name: PlayStation
look: Three-canvas chapter system alternating black, white and PlayStation Blue, weight-300 display, pill CTAs and imagery doing the storytelling.

hero.title: Play has no limits
hero.sub: A custom eight-core processor, a solid-state drive that removes loading entirely, and a controller that lets you feel the difference between gravel and grass.

features.title: Built for the next decade
features.sub: Every component chosen so the loading screen stops existing.

items.title: Custom silicon
items.body: Eight cores at 3.5GHz with a GPU sharing the same memory pool, so nothing waits on a copy between them.

items.title: No loading
items.body: An 825GB custom SSD reading at 5.5GB a second. Fast travel across a city map takes under two seconds.

items.title: Haptic controller
items.body: Adaptive triggers with variable resistance, and haptics precise enough to distinguish surfaces underfoot.

items.title: 3D audio
items.body: Object-based positional audio through any headphones, with no additional hardware required.

items.title: 4K at 120fps
items.body: Variable refresh rate and 8K output on supported displays, with per-title performance modes.

items.title: Backwards compatible
items.body: Over four thousand previous-generation titles play, most of them faster than they did originally.

showcases.title: You can feel the surface
showcases.body: Adaptive triggers vary their resistance shot to shot, and the haptics are precise enough that gravel, grass and wet tarmac each feel different through the grips. It sounds like a marketing line until you drive on all three.

showcases.title: Four hundred games, one subscription
showcases.body: A rotating catalogue of four hundred titles across three tiers, including day-one releases from our own studios. Cloud streaming on the top tier, so a title can be started on the console and finished on a laptop.

gallery.title: GAMES
gallery.sub: Out now and coming soon across every genre.

testimonial.quote: My son and I finished a co-op campaign in a fortnight. He is nine and I am forty-one and neither of us waited more than three seconds for anything to load. That is the whole generational leap, right there.
testimonial.name: Owen Pryce

pricing.title: NOVA PLUS
pricing.sub: Three tiers. Cancel any time and keep anything you bought outright.

tiers.name: PREMIUM
tiers.desc: Adds cloud streaming and the classics.

items.a: Over four thousand previous-generation titles are supported, and most run at a higher and steadier frame rate than they originally did. Disc versions need the disc edition of the console.

items.q: What is the difference between the tiers?
items.a: Essential is online play and two monthly games. Extra adds the four-hundred-title catalogue. Premium adds cloud streaming and the classic catalogue. All three include online multiplayer.

items.q: Can I upgrade a game I already own?
items.a: Yes, for most cross-generation titles, at no cost. The upgrade appears in your library automatically rather than needing to be claimed.
Catalogue titles stop being playable, but anything bought outright — including monthly games claimed while subscribed — stays in your library permanently.

cta.title: PLAY HAS NO LIMITS
cta.sub: Nova 5 is available now. Free next-day delivery, and a 30-day return window.

notes: The page rhythm is a three-canvas chapter system — black, white and PlayStation Blue bands alternating down the page. The colour change is the section divider.
Blue is the universal primary CTA as a full pill. Commerce orange is reserved strictly for buy and pre-order actions, never for a general secondary.
The display tier runs at weight 300 with slightly positive tracking, which is where the airy editorial voice comes from. Bolding it collapses the brand.
Radius is role-based: pills for every CTA, 8px for product cards and feature panels, 4px for inputs.
Imagery occupies 60–90% of each section. The chrome exists to frame game art, not to compete with it.
